The test image shows a cauliflower leaf with multiple discrete brownish/reddish lesions scattered across the blade, with clear leaf venation visible. The spots appear circular to irregular in shape with necrotic appearance. This pattern strongly suggests Alternaria Leaf Spot. Let me check one reference image to confirm.

The reference image shows Alternaria damage presenting as browning on the cauliflower curd, but Alternaria also commonly affects leaves.

Comparing the test image features:
- **Discrete, scattered circular/irregular brownish spots** across the leaf blade
- Spots with necrotic centers and defined edges
- Leaf venation clearly visible (white midrib intact)
- No V-shaped margin lesions (rules out Black Rot)
- No water-soaked soft tissue collapse (rules out Bacterial Soft Rot)
- No yellow patches with downy/fuzzy growth on underside (rules out Downy Mildew)

The pattern of multiple discrete, circular-to-irregular brown lesions scattered across a cauliflower leaf is the hallmark presentation of **Alternaria Leaf Spot** (*Alternaria brassicicola/alternata*), which causes target-spot-like necrotic lesions on brassica leaves.
